transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-04-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Miguel Santos, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Ethan Cole, Marisa Lowe, Dinesh Patel, Sophie Hart (Lakemist)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to map security constraints and ops requirements for a trading advisory proof-of-concept; primary controls around residency, keys, and log retention.

[00:00:05] Miguel Santos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Miguel, AE for Redwood. Priya, our SE, is on the line. Quick go-round?
[00:00:12] Ethan Cole: Hi, Ethan here, I'll kick off — head of platforms at Lakemist. We've got Marisa CISO, Dinesh ML, Sophie compliance.
[00:00:20] Marisa Lowe: Morning. We're looking at inference hosting for advisory models, must be GDPR-friendly and we have some HIPAA adjacent data flows for certain signals.
[00:00:30] Priya Nair: Thanks, Marisa. Can you outline the must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
[00:00:35] Dinesh Patel: Must-have: all EU PII stays in EU; for some US customers we need US-only; so we need per-tenant region lock. Also, we need customer-managed KMS — we can't hand keys off.
[00:00:47] Sophie Hart: And logs, we cannot retain raw messages longer than 7 days for product X, and any PII must be redacted in persistent logs. Also audit evidence for model versioning is required.
[00:00:59] Miguel Santos: Ok — region locking and CMK (customer-managed keys) are common asks. Redwood has Hosted, Dedicated, Private options — short primer: Hosted is fastest to start, but keys are platform-managed unless you use our private option with KMS integration. Dedicated gives more isolation and dedicated GPU pools; Private is full VPC/on-prem with customer keys.
[00:01:20] Ethan Cole: What's the difference practically for us on logs? For Hosted, do logs leave our region?
[00:01:26] Priya Nair: By default hosted control plane may be multi-region, logs are stored in region tied to the request but some metadata for telemetry may be global unless you select region-locking. For strict legal controls we usually recommend Dedicated with region-locking enabled, or Private for the highest control.
[00:01:44] Marisa Lowe: We need proof — like tamper-evident logs and the ability to scope logs to not include raw prompt text. Can Redwood redact at ingest?
[00:01:52] Priya Nair: Yes, we have ingest redaction hooks and prefix/KV caching can be configured to avoid storing PII in long-term logs. Redaction isn't perfect automatic; we provide filtering pipeline examples. We'll share the redaction runbook.
[00:02:07] Dinesh Patel: One follow-up — latency matters. Our model serving needs sub-120ms p50 for small seq lengths. If we go Dedicated with region-locking, does that impact throughput or latency?
[00:02:18] Priya Nair: Good question. Dedicated gives you pinned GPUs so latency is more predictable; region-locking itself doesn't add much latency but reduces fallback options. If a node in EU is saturated, we can't fall back to US; that could increase p95 if capacity planning is tight. We recommend autoscaling + reserved burst capacity to avoid that.
[00:02:36] Sophie Hart: About keys — we require HSM-backed keys and auditable key usage logs. Can Redwood support Cloud KMS with BYOK or HSM escrow?
[00:02:45] Miguel Santos: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM escrow patterns. For Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. We'll attach our Keystore options doc.
[00:02:56] [crosstalk]
[00:03:00] Ethan Cole: On model provenance — auditor will want to see which model version served each request and hash of model artifact; can that be in the evidence bundle?
[00:03:08] Priya Nair: We tag requests with model_version and model_hash and persist a minimal evidence bundle per request when requested (size tradeoff). This can be configured per-route.
[00:03:18] Marisa Lowe: Are those evidence artifacts stored encrypted under our CMK?
[00:03:23] Miguel Santos: Yes, if you're on a CMK config we encrypt stored evidence under customer key. We'll show an example in the security deck.
[00:03:30] Dinesh Patel: Ok, bench — we want a short run with synthetic traffic to test p50/p95 and validate redaction. Can Redwood do a 2-hour anonymized benchmark on EU-only infra?
[00:03:40] Priya Nair: Yep, we can arrange a short bench in an EU region, using a sandbox Dedicated pod or Private evaluation depending on the controls you want. For Hosted it's easier but less isolated.
[00:03:51] Sophie Hart: Our compliance team also wants to know retention windows and how to set per-route retention.
[00:03:56] Priya Nair: We expose retention policies per-route: e.g., 0 days, 7 days, 90 days. For stricter controls we can mark some routes as no-persist and redact at ingest.
[00:04:06] Marisa Lowe: Legal also asked about subpoena and legal hold — if there's a legal hold, can we extend retention for a tenant without affecting others?
[00:04:13] Miguel Santos: Yes, retention policies are tenant-scoped. We also have legal-hold controls to freeze deletion for specified tenants/cases. We'll include audit log examples.
[00:04:22] [00:20:02] Ethan Cole: Quick question on SLA — Dedicated what's the uptime and latency guarantees?
[00:20:08] Miguel Santos: Our Dedicated contracts include an SLA with 99.9% availability and latency SLOs that we commit to for typical seq lengths; exact numbers vary by commitment level. We'll pull the SLA doc and pricing tiers.
[00:20:20] Marisa Lowe: What about staff access — who at Redwood can access logs and request data? Need RBAC and breakglass procedures.
[00:20:28] Priya Nair: RBAC is enforced in the control plane and we have privileged access reviews and breakglass with audit trail. For Dedicated we can limit Redwood support to metadata-only access, with customer consent for full session access. For Private, you can revoke support access entirely.
[00:20:44] Dinesh Patel: Any pitfalls to watch for in the POC? We want to avoid leakage of training signals into logging and ensure KV cache isn't persisted in central logs.
[00:20:52] Priya Nair: We'll disable KV cache persistence for the POC or configure ephemeral caches. Also include token-level filters and prompt templating to avoid raw PII in prompts. We'll share a checklist.
[00:21:03] Ethan Cole: Competitor note — we've seen BigCloudAI promise region-locking but their audit evidence was shallow, that's why we reached out.
[00:21:12] Miguel Santos: Understood. We'll send sample evidence and a short case study of a bank using dedicated region-locked deployment.
[00:21:20] Sophie Hart: One more on encryption in transit — do you support TLS mutual auth between our VPC and Redwood Private?
[00:21:27] Priya Nair: Yes, mutual TLS and VPC peering plus private endpoints supported for Private. For Dedicated we offer VPC options and private networking.
[00:21:35] [00:40:00] Marisa Lowe: If we go forward we'll need an internal runbook for incident response and rollback of model versions — does Redwood provide that?
[00:40:07] Miguel Santos: Yes, we have runbooks for canary rollbacks, automated fallback to smaller models, and playbooks for incident response. We'll include the operations runbook.
[00:40:18] Dinesh Patel: For the benchmark, can Redwood simulate 90 concurrent sessions with varying seq lengths? We'll upload a script.
[00:40:25] Priya Nair: Absolutely — send the script and we'll run it in a sandbox. We'll also provide a run summary with p50/p95/p99 and cost estimate.
[00:40:34] Ethan Cole: Timeline — we'd like POC in April, decisions by mid-May to align with next quarter planning.
[00:40:40] Miguel Santos: Sounds doable; we'll aim to run the bench week of April 12th and follow up mid-April with results.
[00:40:49] [00:50:00] Miguel Santos: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/HIPAA one-pager, security deck, keystore options, and the ops runbook; Priya will set up the bench; Lakemist will share request patterns and retention matrix. Any objections?
[00:50:15] Sophie Hart: No objections, just need the docs for legal review.
[00:50:20] Marisa Lowe: We'll review and come back with a focused list of evidence items.
[00:50:25] Miguel Santos: Great. I'll send the materials and a calendar invite for the benchmark. Thanks everyone.
[00:50:31] Ethan Cole: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:50:34] [END]
